newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds surge after Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds surge after Greenspan comments.

text.p: Argentine bonds were sharply higher late morning Friday, boosted by expectations that U.S. interest rates will be raised at the most only one time in coming months.

The surge in prices followed rallies in other markets after statements by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan late Thursday in which he said the most likely path of the U.S. economy is of "moderate growth and low inflation."

"Everything is fantastic in the market," said a trader at a local bank, adding that there were even purchases by some domestic and foreign funds which have remained on the sidelines in recent weeks on U.S. interest rate uncertainty.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/2 to 92-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was $0.40 higher at 115.55.
Argentina's Par Brady bond due 2023 was the biggest gainer, rising more than a point to 66-6/8. Its yield fell 14 basis points to 9.40 percent.
Another trader said there was very busy activity earlier but trade slowed slightly late in the morning.
